title: AI Governance Lead
description: Role Summary Own the design and execution of the enterprise AI governance program. Build the standards, policies, and procedures that govern how AI use cases and models move from idea to production. Structure the governance roadmap across intake, classification, value assessment, and control design. Stand up use case governance and model governance functions, define the target state for AI governance across the organization, and drive an implementation plan with clear monitoring, prioritized against engineering delivery timelines. Key Responsibilities Governance Framework Design Author and maintain AI governance standards, policies, and procedures covering the full lifecycle of AI use cases and models Design the governance roadmap organized into intake, classification, value assessment, and control design stages Define risk tiers and controls proportional to use case risk (e.g., low/medium/high risk classification tied to required controls) Use Case Governance Build the intake process for new AI use cases: how requests enter the pipeline, what information is captured, who reviews them Establish classification criteria (risk level, data sensitivity, regulatory exposure, business criticality) Design value assessment methodology to prioritize use cases against cost, risk, and business impact Define control requirements per classification tier (documentation, testing, sign-off, monitoring) Model Governance Establish model risk management practices: validation, documentation, versioning, approval gates Define requirements for model cards, testing evidence, bias/fairness checks, and performance monitoring Set standards for third-party and open-source model vetting Target State & Team Build Define the target state for AI governance: what "good" looks like, what the organization should expect from the function Design the governance team structure, roles, and operating model Set RACI across governance, engineering, legal, risk, and business stakeholders Implementation & Monitoring Build a phased implementation plan with milestones and owners Prioritize governance rollout in sequence with engineering platform and architecture delivery Establish monitoring and reporting: KPIs, compliance tracking, exception handling, escalation paths Run periodic reviews of the governance program's effectiveness and adjust as needed Required Qualifications Combined minimum of 10 years' higher education and/or operational/business analytics/systems development experience Demonstrated experience building a governance framework or program from the ground up in a large or complex organization Working knowledge of model risk management practices (e.g., SR 11-7 or equivalent) and how they extend to AI/ML systems Experience designing intake, classification, and risk assessment processes for technology or data initiatives Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, legal, compliance, and business teams Strong written communication skills; able to produce policy documents, standards, and executive-level reporting Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (risk, business, computer science, law, or similar); advanced degree a plus but not required in place of experience Preferred Qualifications Direct experience with AI-specific regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001) and applying them practically Prior experience standing up or scaling a governance team, including hiring and role design Familiarity with MLOps and model deployment pipelines, enough to design controls that don't bottleneck engineering Experience with generative AI governance specifically (prompt/data leakage risk, hallucination controls, third-party LLM vendor risk) Certifications such as CRISC, CISA, or AI governance-specific credentials Experience in a regulated industry (financial services, healthcare, insurance) Skills Required Policy and standards writing Risk classification and control design Stakeholder management across technical and non-technical audiences Program/project management (roadmap building, milestone tracking, prioritization) Working knowledge of ML lifecycle and model development practices Data literacy: able to read model documentation, validation reports, and technical risk assessments Facilitation and negotiation, particularly balancing governance rigor against engineering velocity #LI-JB3 M&T Bank is committed to fair, competitive, and market-informed pay for our employees. The pay range for this position is $123,600.00 - $206,000.00 Annual (USD). The successful candidate’s particular combination of knowledge, skills, and experience will inform their specific compensation. Location Buffalo, New York, United States of America

title: Director, Data Governance (REMOTE, WA)
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Are you a curious builder who thrives in a fast-moving, data-driven execution role, curious about how AI can turn quality data into real, operational trust?   Veeam's business runs on data flowing from four source systems, v-Power for Sales, Marketo for Marketing, NetSuite for Finance, and Workday for HR, through a governed Databricks Lakehouse to certified outputs consumed by Tableau dashboards and AI agents. The Senior Director, AI-Ready Data Governance has authored the strategy for how this gets governed: a federated, pragmatic model, central standards, distributed ownership, sequenced by outcome so scope is committed on evidence rather than ambition. Continuous, agent-driven scoring keeps watching a certified object's quality on an ongoing basis, well past the moment of sign-off.   This is a builder and execution role for a deep subject matter expert, with full autonomy to move fast and deliver results. You will lead highly complex, high-visibility initiatives, shape the approach to problems that arrive ambiguous, and influence organizational direction through the standards you set. The strategy, mission, and vision are set. The job is to run Databricks Unity Catalog as the technical backbone and Atlan as the business-facing catalog on top of it, build the certified Bronze-to-Silver-to-Gold pipeline domain by domain, and make certification, lineage, and continuous scoring real enough that governance becomes a standing rhythm rather than a one-off exercise. AI tooling is moving fast enough that the sequence of what gets built when will keep shifting. What does not shift is the outcome bar: certified data, a live trust score behind it, and a named owner for both.   This is a job for someone who is curious by default. Someone who would rather have an agent draft the first pass of a lineage map than wait for a meeting about it, who gets energy from ambiguity because the pace of AI tooling means the plan will keep changing, and who treats data quality as something they are personally accountable for at every level, source system to dashboard to agent output, ahead of whatever a report tells them after the fact.    What You’ll Do Run Databricks Unity Catalog and Atlan as the technical and business-facing backbone of certification, domain by domain Stand up continuous, agent-driven scoring behind certified data: a live trust score that keeps evaluating after certification, with an automated action attached to it Own the executive intelligence reporting that gives leadership a real, current answer to how much of Veeam's data can be trusted right now, and why Register and govern the AI agents that consume Veeam's data, and use agentic tools yourself, daily, to do the work faster. Align diverse business domain and data owners across Sales, Marketing, Finance, and HR on a defined set of standards. title: Lead Director - AI Governance Engineering
description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Position Summary AI adoption across the organization is accelerating, and existing governance processes can add cycle time and rely heavily on manual review. We are building an AI Governance Engineering capability to modernize governance through automation—shifting from approval-heavy workflows to registration-driven workflows with built-in controls, and continuous observability. As Lead Director, AI Governance Engineering, you will create and lead a lean engineering team responsible for delivering governance-as-code: platform-agnostic SDKs, APIs, and automated controls that help teams move faster while ensuring responsible AI guardrails are consistently enforced. Key Responsibilities Automated Use Case Intake & Risk Classification Design unified intake APIs and user experiences that reduce friction and automatically populate metadata and integrate with application registration and provisioning workflows Implement dynamic intake flows for ML, Generative AI, and agentic use cases. Deliver automated inherent risk scoring and risk-based routing to provisioning and monitoring workflows. Governance-as-Code Toolkits Partner with AI Governance Data Scient to develop a platform-agnostic Python/SDK offering automated governance controls such as bias, drift, and AI safety testing. Integrate governance checks into CI/CD pipelines so evidence is generated during development. Enterprise Model & Use Case Registry Integration Enable event-driven ingestion of intake data and model artifacts into the enterprise registry. Support automated generation of audit-ready compliance artifacts and APIs for reviewers and auditors. Self-Service Enablement & Automation Expand policy-based routing for low- and high-risk AI use cases. Automate proof-of-concept lifecycle patterns and accelerate access to approved AI environments. Governance for Agentic Automation Establish execution safety patterns for internal AI agents, including permission-scoped actions. Partner with information security to implement runtime guardrails such as prompt filtering, data protection controls, and real-time observability. Leadership & Collaboration Build and lead a small, high-impact AI Governance Engineering team. Partner with AI platform teams, governance, security, and privacy partners to embed technical controls into development workflows. Define and track outcomes such as reduced intake complexity, faster cycle times, and improved governance transparency. Required Qualifications Experience leading software or platform engineering teams. Strong system architecture skills across APIs, automation, CI/CD, and data platforms. Experience building developer-facing tools such as SDKs, templates, or automation frameworks. Familiarity with ML and Generative AI lifecycles and how governance controls can be validated through automation. Ability to translate governance or risk requirements into scalable technical solutions. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Responsible AI concepts such as fairness, transparency, explainability, and auditability. Experience integrating automated quality gates into Git-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines. Background working in regulated or high-trust technology environments. Education Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Analytics, Engineering, or related discipline. Master's degree preferred What Success Looks Like AI intake processes are simpler, faster, and largely automated. Engineering teams have reusable SDKs and templates that make responsible AI the default. Validation of controls shifts from self-reporting to automated checks and evidence. Centralized observability provides real-time insight into AI usage, performance, and risk. If you are excited about building trusted AI systems through practical engineering, we encourage you to apply—even if you do not meet every qualification listed. We value collaboration, learning, and curiosity. description: About Gusto At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.   All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .   AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. Head of Risk & Money Services At Gusto, we help more than 500,000 small businesses create great places to work for their people. We do this through modern payroll, employee benefits, expert HR, and financial services. We are searching for a seasoned financial services operator and regulated-domain leader to own one of Gusto's most consequential customer-facing functions: Risk & Money Services. This role sits within CX and Gusto's Financial Services organization and reports directly to the Head of Financial Services. Every dollar that moves through Gusto's platform — payroll being delivered on time, wages being deposited into Gusto Wallet, cash advances being issued, disputes being resolved — carries real financial and regulatory weight. This team makes real-time, high-stakes decisions on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, BSA/AML compliance, whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time, and whether a fraud signal warrants action. The financial impact of individual calls is material. title: Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint
description: About Teramind Teramind is a global leader in workforce intelligence, insider risk management, and data loss prevention. Used by thousands of companies across 60+ countries, our platform gives organizations the visibility to protect their people, their data, and their operations. We sit at the intersection of three converging markets - Insider Risk, DLP, and Workforce Analytics - and we are one of the few players that spans all three on a unified behavioral data layer. The Teramind Endpoint Agent is one of the key differentiators of our platform. It runs on hundreds of thousands of endpoints across Windows, macOS, and Linux, capturing the behavioral signal that powers our detection, DLP enforcement, analytics, and AI. The depth and quality of what the Agent sees is a primary reason customers choose Teramind over the alternatives - and the product leader who owns it plays a pivotal role in the company's success. About the Role We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the Teramind Endpoint Agent, and the AI Usage Control capabilities built on top of it, end to end. You will be the single accountable product leader for the roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of the Agent organization - approximately half of Teramind engineering, working across operating systems, low-level platform components, and the server-side telemetry pipeline. This is a pivotal role. The Agent is one of the strongest competitive moats Teramind has, and the next chapter of the product strategy depends on what we build into it. You are coming in to bring product rigor, customer insight, prioritization discipline, and technical judgment to a team that is capable of shipping world-class endpoint technology. AI Usage Control is one of the most important things you will build here. Companies have spent twenty years governing what employees do with sensitive data, and they now have a second workforce: AI agents reading files, calling tools, and executing commands on the same machines, with none of the accountability. Nobody has worked out what supervising them looks like, and much of it never touches the network, so the endpoint is the only place you can see it. You will own that end to end. You will sit alongside other product managers, reporting to the VP of Product. Together, you own Teramind's product surface area. What You Will Own The Agent roadmap across all platforms. Windows, macOS, Linux, and the platforms after them. You decide what ships, in what order, and why, balancing customer demand, platform modernization, performance, and security hardening on one prioritized backlog. The endpoint layer of AI Usage Control . Detecting AI that never touches the network - native desktop clients, IDE-embedded assistants, terminal-based coding agents, AI-native Teramind | Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint browsers, and local models running offline - and capturing the prompts, pastes, uploads, and agent-executed commands that browser and network DLP cannot see. Translating business vision into engineering reality . You turn signals from executives, sales, customers, competitors and the engineering org into a coherent technical roadmap. You are the interpreter between “we need to detect AI exfiltration” and “here is how we instrument the endpoint to see it.” Building for the enterprise: bulletproof and undetectable . Enterprise customers expect the Agent to be invisible to end users, resilient against tampering, and reliable in conditions that break weaker products. You own the roadmap that keeps it that way. Performance, footprint, and reliability. Every CPU cycle, megabyte and battery percent we consume is felt by the end user and argued about by the customer's IT team. You set and defend the performance bar. Define, measure, and meet product KPIs. Adoption, rollout velocity, deployment success rate, crash rates, detection coverage, time-to-patch on OS changes. You set the numbers and hold the team and the company to them. Industry and ecosystem relationships. Microsoft, Apple, the Linux ecosystem, MDM vendors, and the major AV and EDR vendors. You represent Teramind in technical conversations where the agent's architecture is the subject. Who You Are 5+ years of product management experience , with at least 3 owning a technical platform, SDK, agent, or systems-level product. This is a senior IC seat: influence without headcount. Technical depth is non-negotiable . You do not need to write C++, but you should reason about Windows architecture, macOS system extensions, and the trade-offs between Endpoint Security and Network Extension frameworks. You can push back credibly in a design review. You understand how AI actually runs on a computer . A hosted model in a browser tab, a native desktop client, an IDE-embedded assistant, a CLI coding agent, and a local model under Ollama are five different detection problems, and several are invisible to anything watching the network. You know why, and you know what an audit trail for an autonomous agent has to capture. Endpoint or systems background. You have shipped endpoint security (EDR, EPP, XDR), monitoring or management agents, OS-level tools, or systems software. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender, Tanium and similar are directly relevant. Pure SaaS and application PMs without systems exposure will struggle here. You think in outcomes, not features. Success is “95% of customers roll out a new agent version within 30 days,” not “shipped version 27.0.” You are comfortable with security trade-offs. Visibility versus privacy, tamper protection versus usability, cloud processing versus on-device intelligence. You can hold the attacker's perspective and the IT buyer's perspective in the same conversation. You work with AI, not just about it. You use AI in your own practice, prototyping to pressure-test concepts before spending engineering cycles, and evaluating model behavior rather than trusting vendor claims. You bring rigor, and you write. PRDs, decision memos, prioritization frameworks, release cadence, credible engineering-facing specs. In a distributed team, writing is how product management scales. Nice to Have Engineering background earlier in your career: systems, kernel, driver, or low-level platform work Windows Filter Drivers, Minifilters or WFP; macOS Endpoint Security or Network Extensions; Linux eBPF, kernel modules or userspace agents MDM ecosystems (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, Kandji) Insider risk, DLP, or behavioral analytics Local model runtimes and on-device inference (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) Agentic AI: tool calling, MCP, and autonomous coding or workflow agents AI governance, AI security, or shadow AI discovery products EDR and AV co-existence and exclusion lists at scale Why This Role Endpoint agents are having a moment. The convergence of insider risk, DLP, AI, and hybrid work is making the endpoint the most strategically important surface in enterprise security and workforce intelligence. Teramind's Agent is one of the deepest data-collection engines in the market - we see things the rest of the category does not - and it is one of the strongest competitive moats we have. You are coming in to take a genuinely differentiated technical platform and make it the backbone of the next generation of workforce intelligence. The engineering talent is here. The customer demand is here. The strategic priority is here. Your role is pivotal to where Teramind goes next. Interested? We'd love to hear what you have shipped, what you have owned, and why this role fits what you want to do next. Send us your resume and a short note. Compensation Additional Information About Us At Teramind, we're pioneering a predictive, AI-driven approach to safeguarding organizations' people, data, and operations. As a global leader in user behavior analytics, insider risk management, and workforce intelligence, we empower businesses to transform data into a strategic asset - delivering clear visibility, control, and proactive protection across digital environments. We're open to hiring in just about every country in the world! Feel free to apply even if you don't live in the country listed in the job description. Benefits This is a remote job. Work from anywhere! We’ve been thriving as a fully-remote team since 2014. To us, remote work means flexibility and having truly diverse, global teams. Additionally: • Collaboration with a forward-thinking team where new ideas come to life, experience is valued, and talent is incubated. • Competitive compensation • Career growth opportunities • Flexible paid time off • Laptop reimbursement • Ongoing training and development opportunities Our Recruitment Process We don’t expect you to check every box on the list.
